title: FORCA: A Force-Aware Coding Agent for Contact-Rich Robot Manipulation
why: A-type embodied coding-agent harness: Claude-based coding agent writes/revises Python robot programs that consume RGB-D and wrist F/T, using between-rollout inspection of force records and visual outcomes for contact probing and force-responsive control—no demos, task-specific training, or simulation.
mechanism: FORCA coding agent loop: generate Python program with F/T-aware contact probing skills → execute on UR5e without querying the LM mid-rollout → inspect force+visual records → diagnose and revise motion/force-feedback logic (≤20 rollouts / 4h), then freeze program for repeated trials.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported real-robot (UR5e + wrist F/T + RealSense D455; Claude Fable 5): five contact-rich tasks; vision-only coding-agent ablation; drawer/door-handle report translational/rotational grasp error and success over 10 frozen-program trials (Table I); qualitative contact-probing rollouts in Fig. 4. Exact SR numbers not transcribed beyond abstract claim of effectiveness across three contact forms.
evidence_locator: arXiv abs cs.RO; HTML v1 §III Method (rollout loop), §IV-A setup (hardware/agent), §IV-B drawer/door results
retrieval_notes: Verified abs + HTML method/experiments. Announced Mon 26 Oct 2026 arXiv /new (cs.RO). No GitHub/project URL on abs or HTML. No PDF.

title: LogLook: Execution-Grounded Memory for Frontier-Model Robot Planners
why: A-type harness-memory for frontier VLM robot planners: execution-grounded memory (execution log + selective frame lookup) so a frozen frontier planner tracks what it has done/learned and chooses where to look—separates memory bookkeeping from planner attention under token cost.
mechanism: LogLook memory: keep an execution log and prior notes; planner queries frames only where it expects change; demonstration frames retrieved by note rather than full video dump. Planner is a frontier VLM; executor can be learned π0.5 or motion planner (memory-swap setup).
evaluation_signal: Author-reported closed-loop on RoboMME (Franka Panda sim; 16 tasks / 800 test episodes): memory-swap vs MemER/FrameSamp/Oracle/per-chunk; ablations note-only vs execution-grounded; per-task success tables (Table 2/7) and full-benchmark §4.4. Exact aggregate SR not transcribed beyond per-task counts in HTML.
evidence_locator: arXiv abs cs.RO; HTML v1 §3 Method, §4.1 setup (RoboMME), §4.2–4.4 memory swap/ablations/full bench; project page linked from HTML
retrieval_notes: Verified abs + HTML. Project page https://bingaochen.github.io/Astra-on-RoboMME (no GitHub on abs). Announced Mon 26 Oct 2026.

title: If at First You Don't Succeed, Backtrack: Lightweight Recovery for Frozen VLAs
why: A-type execution-monitor/recovery harness over frozen VLAs: tiny failure head on internal activations triggers pause→retrace→retry without recovery demos, retraining, or a second inference model—fits frozen-VLA + harness recovery family (cf. FastHarness).
mechanism: Backtrack: train small failure-prediction head (0.48–0.88% param overhead) on outcome-labeled rollouts of a frozen VLA; at runtime if failure probability > threshold, controller pauses policy, retraces recent arm motion, returns control to unchanged policy to retry.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported LIBERO (incl. LIBERO-Long) on SmolVLA, π0.5 (flow-matching) and π0-FAST (autoregressive): failure rate −19–48%, success + up to 7.4 pp on long-horizon suite; smaller gains on shorter suites where base success already 85–99%; MetaWorld controller configs and ablations §5. Simulation only.
evidence_locator: arXiv abs cs.RO; HTML v1 §3 Method (failure head, backtrack trigger), §4 setup, §5 Results (recovery/detection/ablations)
retrieval_notes: Verified abs + HTML. No project GitHub on abs (HTML references huggingface/lerobot as dependency only). Announced Mon 26 Oct 2026; also in HF Daily 2026-10-26 keyword screen via related humanoid/boxing neighbors but this ID from arXiv RO listing.

title: UAV-SwarmAgent: Scalable Multi-UAV Reconnaissance and Task Allocation via Code Generation and Vision-Language Reasoning
why: A-type aerial embodied coding-agent harness: NL mission → ground-station agent writes/executes code for multi-UAV route allocation with VLM map grounding and onboard incident verification workers—LLM/VLM tool loop over drone swarm embodiment.
mechanism: Hierarchical multi-agent: operator NL sentence → ground-station coding agent grounds targets on aerial map via VLM, allocates balanced routes to N UAVs in generated code, dispatches worker agents with compact onboard decision model to verify incidents.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported simulation: 4 incident types × 3 foundation models; incident located in 244/255 missions (95.7%); paired scaling study with swarm size; false-alarm/miss analysis §5. Maps derived from UAV-VLA benchmark scenes.

title: HGWM: Hierarchical Graph-Guided World Model for Zero-Shot Object Navigation via Graph Matching
why: A-type agentic ObjectNav harness: LLM room-anchor prior + persistent spatial-semantic graph memory + coarse/fine scoring and LLM direction recommendation before local action—perception–memory–decision loop for zero-shot object navigation.
mechanism: HGWM symbolic predictive nav state: LLM-generated room-anchor goal prior; observation memory as spatial-semantic graph; coarse visual-semantic heading scores (0–10) + fine symbolic graph matching; phase-dependent fusion with LLM direction recommendation then local action.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported HM3D v0.1 / MP3D zero-shot ObjectNav: HGWM 62.6% SR / 31.5% SPL on HM3D vs WMNav 58.1%/31.2% (Table 2; HM3D max/min over 3 runs). Not a controlled shared-backbone comparison. No physical-robot trials.
evidence_locator: arXiv abs cs.RO; HTML v1 §3 Method, §4.3 Main Results Table 2; GitHub+project page from HTML
retrieval_notes: Verified abs + HTML. GitHub https://github.com/itak04/HGWM. Announced Mon 26 Oct 2026. Paper notes reproducibility caveats on controls.

title: Natural-Language to Nav2: Operational Policies for Costmap-Based Navigation
why: A/B-type navigation harness interface: local LLM maps operator NL instructions into JSON operational policies (destinations, spatial constraints, temporal/event conditions) with transactional acceptance, then projects into ROS 2 Nav2 costmaps—LLM outside the control loop but composing the embodied nav stack.
mechanism: NL→JSON policy schema → deterministic structural acceptance (reject preserves prior mission) → three costmap adapters project keepout/soft-cost/object rules into Nav2; NavFn global + DWB local; LLM runs on-prem only when a policy is submitted.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported warehouse/industrial mobile-robot setting measuring structural acceptance vs semantic correctness of policies and navigation under projected costmaps (HTML §1 contributions; detailed numeric tables not fully transcribed).

retrieval_notes: Verified abs + HTML. Project page present; no first-party GitHub for the policy layer (links navigation2 upstream). Announced Mon 26 Oct 2026.

title: Do VLAs Know They Will Fail? Interpretable Success and Failure Patterns in Physical AI Systems

title: Predictive Long-Horizon Progress Modeling with Action-Aware Quantification
why: B-type progress/verification signal for long-horizon manipulation: VLM-decomposed action-aware progress quantification (NimCritic) supplies dense progress for data curation, policy evaluation, and RL—same family as Progress Probes / success detectors.
mechanism: Action-aware quantification: VLM decomposes trajectories into object-level subtasks; weighted action credits for fine-grained progress; NimCritic joint video–progress learning with historical progress perturbation and video–progress alignment.
